skill.description: Turn user-provided personal finance records into a local interactive report with spending, income, transfers and cash movement in English or Chinese. Use for statement-based finance charts and period comparisons, not bank-account actions or investment advice.
skill.summary: Visualize authorized finance records with local charts, reconciled spending, cash movement, and transaction details in English or Chinese.

content.user_title: Visualize Personal Spending and Cash Movement
content.value_statement: Financial records can obscure the difference between personal spending and bank cash movement. This skill creates local interactive reports with confirmed reconciliation and transaction details.
actual_capabilities: Render normalized JSON or CSV records into English or Simplified Chinese reports.
Show spending, income, transfers, and cash movement across daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly periods.
Apply confirmed personal expense shares, exact full-refund mappings, and transfer settlement allocations.
Provide category and merchant charts with searchable transaction details.
Serve reports from memory through a tokenized loopback URL or create an explicitly requested private HTML export.
Generate labeled fictional demonstration data without reading personal records.
limitations: Raw bank CSV requires explicit mapping; PDF extraction depends on authorized tools outside this skill.
Each report supports one currency with two decimal places; automatic currency conversion is not included.
Reports require Python 3.10+ and a modern browser; inputs cannot exceed 25 MiB or 100,000 transactions.
The skill does not connect bank accounts or provide investment advice; agent-host retention still applies to supplied records.

use_cases.title: Review Household Spending
use_cases.description: Compare monthly expense groups and merchants while separating confirmed personal shares from original bank amounts.

use_cases.title: Separate Income from Transfers
use_cases.description: Review supplied income and transfer records without counting unexplained incoming payments as earnings.

use_cases.title: Check Shared Expense Reconciliation
use_cases.description: Inspect confirmed expense shares, full refunds, and repayments while retaining original transaction details.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Fictional Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an English report using only the bundled fictional demo. Show the local viewing URL and do not save an export.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Normalized Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my authorized normalized dataset to show monthly spending and merchant details. Keep the report in memory and identify coverage gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Map and Compare Statement Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm my CSV column mapping, currency, signs, and coverage before rendering. Compare monthly spending and income, keeping uncertain incoming payments as transfers.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile a Bilingual Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply only my confirmed expense shares, full-refund matches, and transfer settlements. Create a Simplified Chinese report showing cash movement and unresolved items, without exporting.

output_examples.input: Fictional USD records show a 100.00 expense with a confirmed 50% personal share.
output: Transaction details retain the original amount and confirmed share.

output_examples.input: Fictional records contain a February purchase of 84.00 and a confirmed full refund of 84.00 in March.
output: The matched purchase contributes no personal spending in February.
February retains the USD 84.00 bank outflow; March retains the USD 84.00 refund inflow.
The original purchase and refund remain available in transaction details.

output_examples.input: Fictional records contain an unexplained incoming payment of USD 65.00.
output: The payment remains an incoming transfer until its purpose is confirmed.
Income excludes this payment; cash movement includes the USD 65.00 inflow.
Report notes identify the unresolved classification.

best_practices: Authorize source records and confirm dates, signs, currency, duplicate evidence, and coverage before rendering.
Apply shares, refund matches, and transfer settlements only after confirmation; document unresolved classifications.
Prefer memory-only delivery; request private exports explicitly and use fictional records for saved screenshots.
anti_patterns: Do not infer refund matches, repayment links, or personal shares from similar names, amounts, or dates alone.
Do not publish report URLs, upload private exports, or place financial records in repositories.
Do not treat incomplete account coverage as a complete financial picture or unknown incoming transfers as income.

faq.question: Which input formats are supported?
faq.answer: The renderer accepts normalized JSON or CSV. Raw bank CSV needs explicit mapping; PDF extraction requires separately available authorized tools.

faq.question: Does the skill connect to my bank?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes user-authorized records and does not collect credentials, connect bank accounts, make payments, or change subscriptions.

faq.question: Is my financial data fully offline?
faq.answer: Rendering uses bundled assets without external requests. Agent hosts may retain supplied records and tool transcripts; the separate update checker contacts GitHub only when invoked.

faq.question: How do spending and cash movement differ?
faq.answer: Spending applies confirmed shares and full-refund matches. Cash movement follows bank dates, excludes internal movements, and applies confirmed transfer settlements.

faq.question: Can I save or translate the report?
faq.answer: Reports support English and Simplified Chinese. An explicit local HTML export includes transaction details and must remain private.

faq.question: Are partial refunds automatically deducted from spending?
faq.answer: No. Full-refund mappings must exactly offset the purchase. Partial or unmatched refunds remain separate and retain their actual bank dates.
